title: Logo Design vs Brand Identity: Which One Do You Need?
h1: Logo design vs brand identity: which one do you need?
description: The difference between a logo, a brand identity and a brand style guide, what each includes, and how to choose the right service for your stage.
intro: Logo design and brand identity are often used as if they mean the same thing, but they are different services. A logo is one mark. A brand identity is the full visual system around it: colors, fonts, image style and rules for using them. Choosing the wrong one either leaves you with a logo that does not work across your materials, or with a large project you did not need yet. This article explains the difference and helps you decide.

faq.q: Is a logo enough for a new business?
faq.a: Often yes, at the start, if it comes with color versions and the right file formats. You can build a fuller identity later.

faq.q: What is a brand style guide?
faq.a: A document that sets out how to use your logo, colors, fonts and images so everything looks consistent.

faq.q: Is brand strategy the same as brand identity?
faq.a: No. Strategy defines your positioning and message; identity is how the brand looks.

faq.q: Can I add a brand identity to an existing logo?
faq.a: Yes. Many designers build an identity around a logo you already have.
A full brand identity is usually a much larger project than a logo, so it normally costs more.
